title: Implemented Growth API and growth change log
reason: Expose decision-quality traffic, search and content data plus a machine-readable change history to the Growth Lab connector
author: claude-code
notes: Bearer-token (GROWTH_AGENT_TOKEN) read-only endpoints reusing the admin GA4 Data API + Search Console integration; adds sessionSource/sessionMedium platform reporting; warm-instance TTL cache. No public page or tracking change.

title: Growth API refusals carry noindex headers; Facebook cover asset committed
reason: Make every /api/growth/* reply consistently no-store + noindex (refusals previously omitted X-Robots-Tag), and put the Facebook Page cover under version control so the social asset is reproducible
author: claude-code
notes: Header change is defence-in-depth only: /api/ is already disallowed in robots.txt and error responses are not indexed. FB-COVER.png becomes publicly reachable at /FB-COVER.png; it is not linked from any page and not in the sitemap.

title: Submitted the German /de/ set to Bing directly; added scripts/submit-to-bing.mjs
reason: Bing had never crawled a single one of the 11 German URLs nine days after launch, so the German pilot had zero impressions in either engine and the 05 Oct decision gate was measuring crawl scheduling rather than German demand. IndexNow cannot reach Microsoft for this host (their endpoint 403s UserForbiddedToAccessSite), so nothing was ever pushing these URLs to Bing.
author: claude-code
notes: All 11 URLs accepted by Bing Webmaster SubmitUrlBatch on 2026-09-13; quota decremented 100->89 daily, 1800->1789 monthly, confirming acceptance. Verified beforehand via GetUrlInfo that all 11 returned the never-crawled sentinel (year 3939). No page, template, content or tracking change - this is a crawl-queue push only. The new script is owner-run and NOT deployed (scripts/ is .vercelignore d). Re-check with: node scripts/submit-to-bing.mjs --prefix=/de/ --verify. Baseline at submission: Bing 0 impressions on /de/ over 28d, Google 0 over 60d, 1 of 11 indexed by Google, GA4 4 pageviews over 60d.

title: German Expo cluster: keyword-aligned titles/descriptions and in-language cross-links (c-langnote)
reason: The German pilot was technically correct but three of six article titles omitted "Belgrad" - including tickets, whose German query ("expo belgrad tickets") is the strongest German-intent term observed in Bing (9 impressions, position 6.3). "Weltausstellung" and "Serbien" appeared in zero German titles or descriptions, all three DACH pavilion descriptions truncated mid-sentence, and the only English-to-German internal link was a two-letter "DE" header chip carrying no anchor text.
author: claude-code
notes: Titles now all lead with "Expo 2027 Belgrad". what-is-it description now names Weltausstellung (as the contrast it genuinely is - this is a Specialised Expo), guide names Serbien. The three DACH i18n.de.summary fields were restructured into two sentences so metaTrim yields a complete first sentence instead of cutting at "der Kategorie..."; their listing `updated` bumped to 2026-09-13 (drives dateModified + sitemap lastmod). New c-langnote pattern added to globals.css first per the Design Law, then used: an in-content cross-link written in the language it points AT, so all 11 German URLs now have a descriptive anchor-text inbound link from their English twin instead of only the DE chip. German hub H1 keeps the editorial line; only the <title> changed. Sitemap unchanged at 156 URLs; hreflang, canonicals and x-default untouched. Build green.
